title: Guided practice: genetics, environment, access, and stress as real contributors
focus: genetics, environment, access, and stress as real contributors
essentialQuestion: How do decisions made now compound over decades, without turning that into fear or blame?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Genetics can affect susceptibility, while environment, stress, discrimination, and access can change exposure and care; risk is not certainty.
Represent long-term health as an interaction among biology, environment, access, behavior, and support; distinguish changeable from fixed factors without assigning blame.
